item.research_question: How to develop a high hardness, high strength–ductility synergy, and excellent corrosion resistance of amorphous lightweight high entropy alloy film?
item.material_system: AlTiVNb high-entropy alloy (HEA) film with nominal composition AlTiVNb (1:1:1:1, at.%)
item.processing_route: High-vacuum magnetron sputtering (JCP500) onto (100) Si wafers; DC power 100 W, Ar flow 30 sccm, pressure 0.5 Pa, work distance 90 mm; film thickness 1.4 μm
item.test_conditions: Nano-pillar compression (height-diameter ratio 2–3, loading rate 5 nm/s); electrochemical corrosion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at room temperature, scanning rate 1 mV/s from −0.5 V to 1.5 V
key_findings: Film density calculated as 5.67 g cm−3, lower than reported similar HEAs.
Average hardness of 5.7 GPa and average modulus of 110.7 GPa.
Compressive strength of up to 3.6 GPa and deformability approaching 58% in nanopillar tests.
Current density of 4.90 × 10−8 A/cm2 and potential of −0.234 V in 3.5% NaCl solution.
Surface shows island structures with approximately several hundred nanometers width and surface fluctuation of 7.5 ± 1.8 nm.
XRD and SAED confirm an amorphous structure with no obvious lattice fringes.
No pitting pits observed on the surface after corrosion testing.
item.mechanism: High strength is attributed to the disordered state, nanostructure, and lattice distortion effect from different atomic sizes; high ductility arises from ductile shear bands and the island structure which disperses deformation energy; excellent corrosion resistance is ascribed to the chemical disorder state, cocktail effect, and homogeneous amorphous structure.
item.future_work: This finding offers new insights into high-performance HEA films with robust mechanical and anticorrosion performances for microelectronic devices and mechanical metamaterials.
quotes: The compression test of the AlTiVNb HEA film nanopillar exhibits a high compressive strength of up to 3.6 GPa and deformability approaching 58%.
The high strength is affected by the disordered state, the nanostructure, and the lattice distortion effect, while the high ductility comes from the ductile shear band and the island structure.
The AlTiVNb HEA film shows a current density of 4.90 × 10−8 A/cm2 and a potential of −0.234 V in the 3.5% NaCl solution, comparable to that of the 316L stainless steel.
